chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Al-Husayn ibn Ishaq, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Abdullah ibn Yahya, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

He said: Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'So they shall be flung into it, they and the erring ones.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'O Abu Baseer! They were a people who portrayed justice with their tongues, then were opposing to something else.'

key_terms.الْغاوُونَ: the erring ones/those who go astray

ai.seo_question: Who are the 'erring ones' mentioned in the verse about being flung into the Fire?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the phrase 'they and the erring ones' in Surah Hud as referring to those who verbally professed justice but acted contrary to it, highlighting the Shia scholarly distinction between mere verbal claim and actual conduct. This hadith from *Al-Kafi* underscores the danger of hypocrisy where outward righteousness masks inner deviation, a key theme in evaluating the sincerity of the faithful.
